name: Nature Communities Fund
summary: Two-year grants for individuals leading community-led habitat creation and restoration projects in public spaces in eight London boroughs, covering their time and project costs, with cohort support. First open call.

amount.note: Two-year grant that funds the grantee's time and project costs.

reporting: Grantees share quarterly light-touch updates, take part in six-monthly progress and cohort reviews, and give an annual evaluation interview.

eligibility.rule: Have the right to reside in the UK
Live in or serve a community in an eligible London borough
Not be in full-time employment or education and dedicate two days weekly
Be ready to start the project in February 2027
Take place in a publicly accessible, free-of-charge space

status.quote: The call for applications is open from 14 October 2026 to 2 December 2026.

applicant_types.quote: this round is for individuals only, but you may apply as an individual that is linked to, or a member of, an organisation

geography.quote: live in or serve a community in one of these London boroughs: Barking and Dagenham, Brent, Hackney, Islington, Lambeth, Lewisham, Newham, Waltham Forest

access.quote: The call for applications is open from 14 October 2026 to 2 December 2026.

window.quote: The call for applications is open from 14 October 2026 to 2 December 2026.

amount.quote: a two-year grant of up to £60,000, with the opportunity to apply for follow-on funding in the third year

consortium_required.quote: We fund individuals rather than groups or organisations.

reporting.quote: reporting: quarterly light touch information sharing 6-monthly progress sharing and cohort review an annual evaluation interview

effort.quote: The call for applications is open from 14 October 2026 to 2 December 2026.
The 10 shortlisted applicants will be invited for a selection panel interview and to give a short presentation covering further details about their project.
Selected applicants will receive a grant offer subject to due diligence, which Afield is required to do by law, and will be asked to provide a reference.

eligibility.quote: have the right to reside in the UK
live in or serve a community in one of these London boroughs: Barking and Dagenham, Brent, Hackney, Islington, Lambeth, Lewisham, Newham, Waltham Forest
not be in full-time employment or education during your proposed project period, and be able to dedicate at least two days a week to your project
be ready to start your project in February 2027
Projects must take place in spaces that are accessible to the public and free of charge.
No. We ask for a two-year commitment because projects of this nature can take a long time to get off the ground

after_award.quote: reporting: quarterly light touch information sharing 6-monthly progress sharing and cohort review an annual evaluation interview
attending monthly cohort sessions facilitated by Afield over the two-year funded period: monthly for six months, frequency thereafter to be decided by cohort
